# Mid fixture draft (fixture-only synthetic)

## Introduction

This report argues that a named supply chain, Inditex, can use sustainability to defend its position, and that the argument still holds when demand falls.

## Drivers of sustainability-centric SCM

Regulation and buyer expectations push Inditex to publish targets, while energy costs make waste reduction pay. The report weights the regulatory driver highest because it binds the chain rather than one supplier.

## Benefits of integrating sustainability

The benefits are lower energy use, fewer returns, and a stronger claim in tenders. The evidence develops the point where a supplier's water use falls and the saving is passed back to the chain.

## Integration to competitive advantage

Integration works when the target, the buying decision, and the audit share one measure. Inditex's tier-one audit is used because it shows the limit as well as the gain: the audit covers fabric but not shipping, so the advantage is real in one part of the chain.

## Recession relevance

In a recession, buyers trade down and the chain's fixed costs matter more. The same integration lowers the cost of a shorter order run, which is where the advantage survives the downturn.

## Conclusion

The judgement is that integration pays in the parts of the chain that are audited, and that the recession tests the claim rather than replacing it.
